issues.claim: A rise after a fall that held a household has no defined arrivals. Since round 3, V06 §3.5.1 (1) (l.1223-1229) passes over each locked or pinned household 'for the next household below it in that order that is neither', and (4) (l.1240-1247) passes over a protected dwelling's last household under any fall that is not a dossier fall, the next household below it leaving in its place. §7.7's precedence (base l.11718-11723) does the same under a dossier fall the unlocked households can meet. After such a fall the town holds the roster's households up to the target, less those that left in a held household's place, plus the held ones above it — no longer the roster's prefix. Yet §4.11's delta demand is 'the suffix of the sequential roster between the old and the new population, §10.2 — prefix-stable' (l.7879-7881), and §10.2's AM-8 says 'a later rise reoccupies the same suffix first' (l.15300-15302). Read as written, a rise past a held household's ordinal adds it a second time while it stands, and never returns the households that left in its place, which lie below the old population. A builder reading the delta as a set (the roster's households up to the new population the town does not hold) builds a different town. V06 §3.6 (1) reads 'the delta demand's households' and states neither reading. §3.21's decline row, T-V6-5, T-V6-6 and T-V6-70 (f) stop at the fall, and no catalogue entry or combination names the decline-then-rise sequence. The path is ordinary: a locked or pinned building on the decline path of a standalone advance that falls and then rises, or a dossier that falls and recovers. A household added twice is a silent wrong count against DR7's bar.
issues.required_change: 1. V06 §3.5.1 (1) adds, after '`households.heldByLock` —': 'A household held so keeps its place and its roster ordinal: the town then holds the roster's households up to the met count less those that left in a held household's place, plus the held ones. At every later epoch the delta demand (§4.11's suffix between the old and the new population) is read over that set — the roster's households up to the epoch's target that the town does not hold, in ordinal order, those that left in a held household's place first (§10.2's AM-8: the same suffix back first). A held household that still stands is never added twice, so the town holds exactly the roster's prefix to the target once the target reaches every held household's ordinal.' 2. V06 §3.21's decline row adds the edge 'a rise after a fall that held a household' with the outcome 'the households that left in its place return first, the held one never added twice (V06 §3.5.1 (1))'. 3. T-V6-70 (f) adds, on H-100: 'then a rise past the held households' ordinals — no household id added twice, the passed-over households back, the town's households the roster's prefix to the new target, the members summing to it within the roster tolerance (DR7's bar)'. 4. END for pipeline: §4.11's delta-demand parenthesis (l.7880) reads 'the suffix of the sequential roster between the old and the new population, §10.2 — prefix-stable, read over the households the town holds where a fall held one (V06 §3.5.1 (1)) — so no survivor's use is withdrawn by arithmetic'.

issues.claim: An absorb whose dossier carries a `population` or an `institutions` value the port cannot read has no safe outcome on a bound map. Round 3 turned both from a refusal (`E_UNKNOWN_SHAPE` before R3-20) into the creation fallback: V08 §2.4's `population` row (l.634: 'empty, or no such integer → the default request of the tier word's rung …, else the one-click default's 5 000'), its `institutions[]` row (l.646: 'a value that is no list (read as absent, noted)'), J-V8.134 (l.3527) and §3.5 step 3 (l.1600-1605). Only the `id` row (l.631) states an absorb-time fallback ('at an absorb the bound document's settlement key'). `population`, `institutions[]`, `name` and `tier` state only the creation value. V08 §3.5's diff (l.1665-1675) then compares the carried facts with the new digest. The settlement row's `population` → `population` makes an epoch whose target is the tier word's default. Every carried institution key now absent makes `remove` with fate `vanished`, closing every dossier-bound use, locked buildings' included (§7.7 item 14). `name` → `rename`. A port epoch is no undo, redo or revert target (V08 §2.7, l.1291), and the next readable dossier raises the population back and reopens each institution (F6). So one unreadable value rewrites the map twice. The same subsection gives the opposite outcome for an unreadable record: when a quarantined record's key cannot be formed, 'every carried institution key absent from the new digest is held — no `remove` — … until a readable dossier arrives' (l.1666-1668). Item 125 (b) asks for 'the generator's own choice, exactly as on a map made without a dossier', and on a bound map made without a dossier nothing changes the population or the institutions. §3.17's rows (l.2643, l.2657), T-V8-61 and §7.7 item 10 state the fallback without the absorb case.
issues.required_change: 1. V08 §3.5's diff, after the quarantine sentence, adds: 'At an absorb, a value of a required key that took its field-table fallback — `population`, `name` or `tier` empty or unreadable, an `institutions` that is no list (V08 §2.4) — makes no change: the carried fact stands. The settlement row compares nothing for that field, and every carried institution key is held, no `remove`, as a quarantined record's are. One `field_fallback` note names the field with "the map kept its record's last value", until a readable value arrives. The field table's fallback values serve a creation.' 2. V08 §2.4's `population`, `name`, `tier` and `institutions[]` rows each add to their fallback cell '— at an absorb, the carried value (V08 §3.5)'. 3. J-V8.134 adds 'at an absorb the carried value stands for every such field, as the `id` row's bound key does'. 4. §3.17's 'the digest and the diff' row and 'the one input and its fallbacks' row add the case 'an absorb whose `population`, `name`, `tier` or `institutions` is empty or unreadable', with the outcome 'the carried value kept, no change, noted `field_fallback`'. 5. T-V8-61 (a) adds: 'on `city-1` after its creation, an absorb whose `population` is emptied and whose `institutions` is an object keeps the carried population and every institution — no epoch, no `remove`, no `rename`, the model digest unchanged — each noted `field_fallback`, and the next readable dossier absorbs as usual'.
